observables.trades_per_min: fills per minute of active window span
observables.first_favored_frac: fraction of events whose first buy is the favorite (p>0.5)
observables.first_tte_s: seconds from first acquisition to window CLOSE (epoch+duration)
observables.completion_rate: fraction of events reaching any matched inventory
observables.t_to_match_s: seconds from first acquisition to first matched inventory
observables.concurrency: max distinct windows open simultaneously that day

changepoint_method.algorithm: multivariate binary segmentation, L2 mean-shift cost on sqrt(event-count)-weighted z-scores
changepoint_method.dominance_filter: keep a change point only if its cost reduction is >= 10% of the largest accepted reduction

verdict_open_extend_complete_vs_compensa.call: SUPPORTED. OPEN -> EXTEND -> COMPLETE -> repeated inventory compression belongs primarily to the EARLY regimes. Across the dominant change point the OPEN/EXTEND half of the motif is unchanged (P(EXTEND) ~constant) while the COMPLETE/compression half collapses: completion rate and the repeated-compression motif fall sharply, terminal residual rises several-fold, and median matched pair cost moves toward $1. Late behaviour is better described as persistent two-sided quoting that is NOT reliably compressed into matched pairs -- i.e. compensated liquidity provision -- and the first TAKER_REBATE and REWARD records in the corpus appear in the late regimes only.
verdict_open_extend_complete_vs_compensa.caveat: Rebate/reward cashflows in /activity are sparse (183 rebate + 20 reward records in 760,817 fills). Absence of rebate records is NOT proof of absence of rebates; the endpoint may simply not surface them. Maker/taker role is UNAVAILABLE, so 'liquidity provision' is inferred from price placement and pair economics only.
